messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Sev2 - streaming tail latency spike detected (p95=1.1s -> 3.8s, p99=4.2s -> 8.0s) for SSE/WebSocket paths in eu-west-1. Proxy timeouts 502/504 increasing, client retries observed. Trace sample IDs: t-9f3a, t-9f4b, t-9f5c. Auto-alerts triggered: streaming.slo.p99, streaming.proxy.5xx

Dina_oncall: acked. I'm on it. Observed customer-facing errors in /v1/stream and /v1/chat/stream. Can someone pull recent proxy logs and router metrics? @evan_sre @harper_eng

Evan_sre: pulling logs now. Early hint: proxy write queues backing up, lots of "write timeout" in proxy logs around 2026-03-15T12:04Z. Also seeing client RSTs and slow consumer backlog. Link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/streams?span=last_30m :mag_right:

Harper_eng: possible causes: client backpressure (slow consumers), bursty seq lengths causing KV cache misses, or a regression in proxy keepalive behavior. If proxies are queuing, restarting a small subset to drain might help. Suggest rolling restart of streaming-proxy in eu-west-1 canary (2 pods) and bump proxy write_timeout to 45s temporarily.

Frank_support: impacted customers: acme-inc (high volume), fastchat-ai (3 incidents), and several smaller tenants showing increased request errors. I'm prepping customer communications. If we enable degraded-mode fallback (polling) for high-latency tenants that could reduce impact.

Ben_db: DB metrics look normal, CPU/mem ok. No hotspot on KV store. Network retransmits on the proxy nodes are up ~3x baseline. My vote: network/proxy or client pacing rather than DB.

Irene_pm: please log mitigation decisions in this thread. Keep me posted on customer-impacted count and ETA for mitigation.

Evan_sre: running canary restart now on two pods (eu-west-1):
```bash
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/streaming-proxy --context=eu-west-1 --selector=canary=true
```
Output: deployment.apps/streaming-proxy restarted

Evan_sre: also bumping write_timeout to 45s via config toggle for eu-west-1 streaming-proxy configmap. Command:
```bash
kubectl -n prod patch configmap streaming-proxy-cfg -p '{"data":{"write_timeout":"45s"}}'
```
Applied. Observability: tail latency graph will show lag for ~30s while new pods warm up.

incident-bot: Auto-alert: canary-restart started, routed 5% traffic to canary pods. Observability link: https://dash.redwood.internal/streams/trace?t=5409876543

Dina_oncall: good. Frank, can you flip degraded fallback for acme-inc and fastchat-ai? That will route them to polling endpoint (non-stream) until streaming is stable.

Frank_support: toggling fallback for acme-inc and fastchat-ai:
```bash
rwdctl feature-flag set customer:acme-inc streaming.degraded true
rwdctl feature-flag set customer:fastchat-ai streaming.degraded true
```
Responses: both toggles applied. Customer-monitor-bot: Notified tenant usage teams for acme-inc and fastchat-ai.

Harper_eng: enabled a temporary per-proxy backpressure limiter to reduce burst queueing (config change pushed). Patch: reduced max_inflight_requests from 2000 -> 800 for eu-west-1 proxies.

Evan_sre: canary metrics look encouraging: p99 for canary pods dropped to ~600ms after restart and config changes. Global p99 trending down from 8s to 1.8s. Rolling restart resumed for remaining pods with conservative cadence.

incident-bot: Metric update: streaming.slo.p99 decreased: 8.0s -> 1.6s over 6m. 5xx rate decreased from 2.1% -> 0.4%.

Ben_db: traced a tail request t-9f5c — client was sending very slow reads, causing proxy buffer retention. We're seeing a multimodal distribution: some tenants have a lot of slow-consumer clients. Longer-term: consider per-tenant streaming timeouts + QoS.

Irene_pm: documented mitigation steps: canary restart, write_timeout bump, reduced max_inflight, toggled degraded fallback for two tenants. Good work. Please prepare a short customer note for acme-inc and fastchat-ai explaining fallback and ETA for re-enable.

Frank_support: pinged customers via support channel, included status and that streaming is degraded and polling is enabled as fallback. acme-inc responded they see improved behavior. fastchat-ai asked for an ETA to re-enable streaming; told them we'll update in 30m.

Harper_eng: I've gated a quick config-revert playbook to re-enable streaming per-tenant after verification. Steps: 1) confirm p99 < 800ms for 10m, 2) revert feature flag, 3) monitor 15m. Command to revert: `rwdctl feature-flag set customer:<id> streaming.degraded false`

Evan_sre: rolling restarts completed. Post-change metrics: p95=220ms, p99=760ms, 5xx ~0.2%. Looks stable for last 9 minutes.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident state changed to: mitigated -> monitoring. All automated health checks passing in eu-west-1.

Dina_oncall: handing off post-mitigation to oncall-sre rotation (next shift). Leaving notes for RCA: collect proxy logs around 12:00-12:10Z, identify client slow-consumer patterns, analyze effect of write_timeout and inflight threshold change. @evan_sre please take lead on RCA?

Evan_sre: will lead. I'll capture traces t-9f3a/t-9f4b/t-9f5c and do a histogram of consumer read latencies. Also propose short term follow-ups: per-tenant streaming throttle, improve backpressure signals to clients, and automated degraded-mode for tenants above a threshold.

Irene_pm: schedule a 1hr RCA session for tomorrow 09:00 UTC, include SRE, serving, product, and support. Add action items: customer communication template, metrics alert tuning (avoid noisy auto-escalation), and runbook update for streaming incidents.

Frank_support: I'll follow up with customers once streaming is re-enabled. Leaving this thread to monitoring. :wave: 

customer-monitor-bot: Noting decreased customer error counts for acme-inc and fastchat-ai. Will continue 1m checks for 1h and escalate if errors return.
